body: Monday, February 16 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information cutoff: 2026-02-16 00:00 UTC. Market figures use completed observations before this date.

Macro Stance: January payrolls rose by 130,000 Bureau of Labor Statistics (.gov) [Feb 13] and headline CPI cooled to 2.4%, less than expected CNBC [Feb 13], but core CPI picked up on firmer services costs Bloomberg.com [Feb 13]. That lets the Fed wait without closing the door: traders boosted bets to 50% for three cuts this year Bloomberg.com [Feb 13]. Mixed — the macro is fine; the equity tape is trading AI-disruption fear.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.40% and the 10Y at 4.04%, a 10Y−2Y spread of +64 bps; over 20 observations the 2Y fell 16 bps and the 10Y 13 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13). The curve is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average, after a bull steepening (both down, 2Y down more). Equities missed the relief: the S&P 500 closed at 6,836.17, down 1.56% over 20 sessions, with the VIX at 20.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

New / Most Important: Senator Tillis will not support confirming the Fed-chair nominee until the DOJ investigation of Powell is done The Hill [Feb 15] — a slower handover keeps the current, patient committee in charge for longer. The limited government shutdown is likely to linger at least 10 days as Congress takes a break The Guardian [Feb 14], adding headline risk but little GDP drag.

Playbook ✓: Own the 5Y at 3.61% as the cleanest expression of the cut repricing (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13), and stay underweight the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ down 3.19% over 20 sessions) against industrials (XLI up 5.06%) until Nvidia reports (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Change the call if a hot core print lifts the 2Y back above 3.56%, its level 20 observations ago (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13).

Macro Stance: Europe is the relative winner of the AI scare. Euro-area GDP rose 0.3% in the latest quarterly estimate European Commission [Feb 13], inflation fell to 1.7% in January Financial Times [Feb 04], and the ECB is extending its longest rate pause since the negative-rate era Reuters [Feb 12] — below-target inflation gives Frankfurt an easing option the Fed lacks.

Activity & Inflation: The STOXX 600 closed at 617.70, up 0.54% over 20 sessions against a 1.56% fall in the S&P 500, while EUR/USD at 1.1868 is up 2.23%, itself a disinflation channel (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Money is following: Europe and Asia led equity fund inflows as the US recorded a weekly outflow Reuters [Feb 13].

New / Most Important: The AI scare has reached European software: Dassault Systèmes plunged 18%, on track for its worst day ever CNBC [Feb 11]. Europe outperforms because it is short software and long banks, energy and industrials — the FTSE 100's 2.06% 20-session gain against the DAX's 1.51% loss shows the mix (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

Playbook ✓: Overweight European banks and domestic cyclicals against US growth; prefer the FTSE 100's value mix to the DAX's export and software tilt, funded from software and China-exposed luxury. Change the view if euro-area inflation turns back up or the fund-flow rotation reverses toward the US for several weeks.

Macro Stance: China heads into the Lunar New Year with deflation easing at the margin but private demand still soft. The policy mix is supportive — moderately loose money, a large grid programme and a trade truce — yet households are not borrowing and housing is still falling. We stay Mixed: policy is putting a floor under activity and markets, but there is no self-sustaining recovery to buy yet.

PMIs & Activity: The latest official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in January Reuters [Jan 30], back in contraction territory. Autos are the visible weak spot: January car sales fell at the fastest pace in nearly two years Reuters [Feb 10], the clearest sign that discount-driven demand is fading. The February PMIs need to show the official index back above 50 before we treat the January dip as noise; until then, read activity as flat at best.

Credit Impulse: January new loans jumped but missed forecasts as weak demand persists Reuters [Feb 13]. The PBOC pledged to keep policy moderately loose State Council Information Office [Feb 11], but credit supply is not the constraint — household and private-sector demand is. Until household lending turns, the impulse flows into financial assets rather than capex, which is why onshore equities have held up better than the activity data.

Property: New home prices extended their decline in January Reuters [Feb 12], and support is becoming more direct: Shenzhen is drafting an $11.6 billion rescue package for China Vanke Reuters [Feb 10]. A state-led backstop for a systemically important developer cuts tail risk for banks and bondholders, but it does not create buyers. Treat a slower pace of decline as the best case for 2026, not a floor, and keep developers out of the portfolio.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: The clearest capex line is the plan to invest 5 trillion yuan in the power grid over five years China Daily Global Edition [Feb 10] — a multi-year order book for transformers, cables and switchgear that does not depend on housing. On trade, Reuters reported Trump paused China tech bans ahead of a Xi summit Reuters [Feb 12], extending the trade truce. The near-term risk is that the summit slips and the bans return.

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng closed at 26,567.12, down 1.72% in the prior session and 1.03% over 20 sessions; the Shanghai Composite ended at 4,082.07, off 0.48% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). In New York, ASHR held at 33.68 (down 0.82% over 20 sessions) while KWEB fell to 32.79 (down 9.87%) and FXI to 38.33 (down 4.17%); USD/CNY slipped 0.95% to 6.9001 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Onshore A-shares and the currency are being managed for stability, while the offshore internet complex is where the selling concentrates.

New / Most Important: The biggest single-company signal is Meituan's warning of a $3.5 billion loss from the food-delivery price war South China Morning Post [Feb 13]. It explains KWEB's 9.87% 20-session drop better than any macro print: the platform names are spending their profits to defend share (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Until a truce among the delivery platforms appears, internet is a margin story, not a growth story.

Playbook ✓: Prefer onshore A-shares (ASHR) and grid-equipment suppliers tied to the 5 trillion yuan programme over platform internet (KWEB). Keep a long-CNY bias against the dollar while USD/CNY trends lower. Upgrade to Bullish on a credit print that beats forecasts with stronger household lending; downgrade if new-home price declines re-accelerate or the tech-ban pause is reversed. ⚠ Divergence: factory-gate deflation eased more than forecast in January Bloomberg.com [Feb 10], which says reflation may arrive faster than the credit data imply.

Macro Stance: Prime Minister Takaichi's election win helped the Nikkei touch 58,000 as the yen and JGBs rallied on the fallout Reuters [Feb 12]. Japan avoided a technical recession but the Q4 rebound missed expectations CNBC [Feb 15], and BOJ hawk Tamura flagged spring as possible timing for a hike Bloomberg.com [Feb 12] — a political mandate plus normalisation is bullish for the yen and domestic financials.

Activity & Currency: The Nikkei 225 closed at 56,941.97, up 5.23% over 20 sessions despite a 1.21% drop in the prior session; USD/JPY fell to 152.82, down 3.64% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Takaichi meets Governor Ueda on Monday Reuters [Feb 13] — the first read on whether the government lets the BOJ hike into a stronger yen.

Playbook ✓: Own the yen against the dollar and Japanese banks over exporters, whose margins a stronger yen compresses. Reverse if the Ueda meeting signals pressure to delay hikes, or if USD/JPY reclaims 158.6, its level 20 sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

Macro Stance: The RBA has turned from easing to tightening: it raised the cash rate to 3.85% after three cuts AP News [Feb 02], and Bullock said it will raise again if inflation becomes entrenched Reuters [Feb 11]. Australia is out of sync with the global easing cycle, which is why the Aussie has outrun the euro, sterling and the yen against the dollar over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD closed at 0.7087, up 5.71% over 20 sessions and 2.47% over five, while the ASX 200 stood at 8,917.60, up 0.63% over 20 sessions after a 1.39% fall in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Higher rates have not broken the banks: CBA posted record first-half earnings on market-share gains Reuters [Feb 10]. The next test is breadth, as 80 companies prepare to report AFR [Feb 15].

Playbook ✓: Stay long AUD against the dollar and own the major banks with deposit franchises, which earn more on a higher cash rate; underweight rate-sensitive retailers and housing-linked names. Change the call if monthly CPI rolls over decisively, or if reporting-season guidance shows the strong currency crushing exporter earnings.

Monetary & Activity: Bankier reports GDP growth accelerated to 4% in Q4 (PKB przyspieszył do 4 procent) Bankier.pl [Feb 12], while January CPI printed 2.2% y/y (inflacja CPI na poziomie 2,2 proc.) StockWatch.pl [Feb 13]. With growth that strong and inflation that low, Gazeta Prawna calls a March rate cut 'a very likely scenario' (bardzo prawdopodobny scenariusz) Gazeta Prawna [Feb 15].

FX & Markets: USD/PLN closed at 3.5493, down 2.12% over 20 sessions, while EUR/PLN was flat at 4.2097; EPOL ended at 37.67 (up 4.2%) and the WIG20TR tracker at 66.80 (up 2.22%) after a 1.68% drop in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Polish bond yields fell below 5%, the lowest in two years (rentowności poniżej 5 proc.) Bankier.pl [Feb 12].

Companies: The EU Court of Justice ruling on WIBOR clauses means 'WIBOR will not be a second franc', per Rzeczpospolita Rzeczpospolita [Feb 12]. Yet Pekao fell 3.35% and PKO BP 2.89% in the prior session, while Orlen is up 8.76% and PGE 10.15% over 20 sessions and CD Projekt is down 14.22% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

Security & New Development: Parliament approved €44bn of EU SAFE defence loans Notes From Poland [Feb 13], a multi-year funding line for domestic arms production. The counterweight is fiscal: Fitch said Poland risks a downgrade if debt is not stabilised Reuters [Feb 10] — a risk EUR/PLN, flat over 20 sessions, is not pricing (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

Playbook ✓: Own Polish duration and the zloty against the dollar into a likely March cut; prefer PKO BP and Pekao on the WIBOR relief and Orlen/PGE on momentum over consumer and gaming names. Change the call if CPI moves back above target or Fitch acts. ⚠ Divergence: the banks sold off hardest despite the favourable ruling — the market may be pricing lower rates into margins faster than loan growth can offset.

Narrative: XLK closed at 139.56, down 4.06% over 20 sessions, with Microsoft down 12.12% and Palantir 25.79% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Reuters maps an AI scare trade running from software to real estate Reuters [Feb 13]: the market now asks who gets disrupted before it asks who benefits.

Reported: Cisco topped estimates but fell 7% on a mediocre forecast CNBC [Feb 11] — a beat without an AI-proof guide gets sold. Oracle is the counter-example, up 12.13% over five sessions though still down 15.65% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

EPS Upside Watch: Estimates rise where AI spending lands as hardware — memory, storage, networking. Apple is the swing name, down 8.03% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13); if its margins absorb higher component costs, it rejoins the winners.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Even Broadcom, a hardware winner on paper, is down 5.2% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Until the scare trade exhausts itself, prefer SOXX's memory and equipment names to XLK's software-heavy mix.

Narrative: XLC closed at 114.58, down 1.40% over 20 sessions: Meta is up 3.06% while Alphabet is down 8.13% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Alphabet's almost $32 billion bond sale shows the platforms now fund AI with debt Bloomberg.com [Feb 10].

Reported: Pinterest sank nearly 17% as tariffs hit earnings CNBC [Feb 13] — smaller ad platforms carry tariff-sensitive merchant budgets the giants can dilute. Netflix closed at 76.87, down 12.70% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

EPS Upside Watch: Meta is the one megacap being paid for its capex; Netflix's de-rating leaves room for a positive surprise if engagement holds, while Alphabet must show its debt-funded spending earns a return.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Credit is happier than equity: bondholders absorbed Alphabet's debt Bloomberg.com [Feb 10] while its shares fell 5.31% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). The equity is pricing diluted returns, not solvency risk — a setup to buy once capex guidance stabilises.

Narrative: XLF closed at 51.65, down 4.81% over five sessions and 5.00% over 20, with Bank of America down 7.04% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). The AI scare jumped to financials — AI fears hit Charles Schwab and other financial stocks Barron's [Feb 12] — and Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Citigroup all plunged more than 5% on Thursday 24/7 Wall St. [Feb 13].

Reported: Fourth-quarter numbers were not the trigger; the sell-off hit between reporting dates, on fears that AI tools compress fee pools in wealth, brokerage and advisory. Goldman closed at 905.14, down 7.25% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

EPS Upside Watch: Trading desks gain from volatility and lower yields support loan demand, but the group is priced on AI and private-credit exposure, so beats will not be rewarded until that fear fades.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The real risk sits in credit, not deposits: Bloomberg reports private credit's software bet is even bigger than it appears Bloomberg.com [Feb 13]. If software borrowers are the AI losers, their lenders are second-order losers — avoid alternative managers and BDCs before the big banks.

Narrative: Energy leads the 20-session sector table: XLE closed at 54.35, up 14.16% over 20 sessions, with Exxon up 14.96% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). The driver is rotation and geopolitics, not barrels — Brent at 67.75 is up only 6.26% over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

Reported: BP suspended its buyback to trim debt and its shares fell 7% Reuters [Feb 10]: European majors are choosing balance sheets over payouts at these prices, which is why the rotation favours XOM and CVX.

EPS Upside Watch: Chevron, up 10.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), is the cleanest Venezuela lever after the US eased sanctions to give oil majors broad scope to operate there Reuters [Feb 13].

⚡ Breaking Convention: OPEC+ leans toward resuming output increases from April Reuters [Feb 13], so the bull case rests on Iran risk rather than supply. Own XLE as a geopolitical hedge, not as a call on oil fundamentals, and trim into any spike.

Narrative: XLI closed at 174.17, up 5.06% over 20 sessions, and Caterpillar is up 19.63% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). The macro anchor is the January ISM manufacturing PMI at 52.6% PR Newswire [Feb 02] — the factory cycle is turning just as AI and grid capex accelerate.

Reported: Siemens jumped on a lifted outlook WSJ [Feb 12], confirming that automation and electrification order books are converting into guidance upgrades. GE closed at 315.41, slightly lower over 20 sessions, while Boeing rose 1.51% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

EPS Upside Watch: Grid and power-equipment suppliers: China alone plans 5 trillion yuan of grid investment over five years China Daily Global Edition [Feb 10], on top of US utility capex plans. Caterpillar's power-generation business gives it the same exposure, and transformer and switchgear makers sit in the same slipstream.

⚡ Breaking Convention: AI-disruption fear has already moved from software into real estate Reuters [Feb 13]; intermediaries in physical industries are the natural next targets. Own capex beneficiaries that build things, not intermediaries that broker them.

Narrative: XLY closed at 116.18, down 5.31% over 20 sessions, as Amazon fell 16.54% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13); AI-spending fears drove Amazon into a bear market MarketWatch [Feb 13]. Tesla is down 4.82% over 20 sessions, so the two largest weights are both drags.

Reported: Airbnb rose on a revenue beat and rosy guidance CNBC [Feb 12], showing that discretionary names with visible demand and no AI threat can still be paid. Nike closed at 63.13 after a 3.32% gain in the prior session, while Home Depot is up 3.14% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
EPS Upside Watch: Travel and experience platforms with pricing power (Airbnb) and housing-repair spending (Home Depot) are the upside pockets; mid-priced restaurants and goods retailers are not.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The consumer is K-shaped: US firms confront a widening gulf as the wealthy spend and budget shoppers struggle Reuters [Feb 11]. That favours luxury travel and big-box value, and squeezes everything in between — the sector average hides two opposite trades.

Narrative: Staples are the AI-scare refuge: XLP closed at 89.51, up 8.67% over 20 sessions, with Walmart up 12.32% and Costco 6.45% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Walmart's results headline the week ahead Reuters [Feb 15], so the group's leadership faces a hard test.

Reported: Coca-Cola forecast modest growth amid demand concerns CNBC [Feb 10] — the brand-owners are guiding to little growth; the money is buying defensiveness and dividend safety. Scale retailers with grocery traffic are the exception.

EPS Upside Watch: Walmart is the upside candidate: in a K-shaped economy where budget shoppers struggle Reuters [Feb 11], it gains trips from both ends of the income distribution. Costco, at 1,018.48 after a 1.96% gain in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), offers the same membership-driven resilience.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The rally is about safety, not growth: an 8.67% 20-session gain for a sector guiding to modest growth is a valuation move (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). That leaves XLP exposed to any AI-relief rotation back into tech — keep the overweight, but tighten stops after Walmart.

Narrative: XLV closed at 157.67, up just 0.45% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13): obesity winners against policy and managed-care losers. Lilly blew past estimates as Zepbound and Mounjaro sales soared CNBC [Feb 04], while Novo Nordisk sank 17% on a bleak 2026 forecast Yahoo Finance UK [Feb 04].

Reported: The split reads as share, not category: Lilly's beat and Novo's guide together suggest volume is moving to Lilly. Lilly closed at 1,040.00, up 0.68% over 20 sessions despite the beat (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13) — the beat was priced in.

EPS Upside Watch: UnitedHealth rose 3.10% in the prior session but sits 13.50% lower over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Managed care now carries low expectations, which is the precondition for upside surprises once medical-cost trends stabilise.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Novo's guidance Yahoo Finance UK [Feb 04] matters beyond Novo: it suggests price erosion in the category, which hurts cash-pay and compounding channels more than Lilly. Healthcare is not a clean AI-scare refuge — policy and pricing risk keep it Mixed.

Narrative: XLB closed at 53.31, up 8.88% over 20 sessions, led by precious metals: gold settled at 5,046.30, up 9.14%, and Newmont rose 6.50% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Gold rose more than 2% as soft inflation rekindled rate-cut hopes Reuters [Feb 13].

Reported: Miners are reporting with gold at 5,046.30, and Newmont's 9.09% five-session gain shows the market paying for cash generation (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Freeport is up 4.80% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

EPS Upside Watch: Copper producers: copper at 5.79 is down 2.61% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), yet it is the AI data-centre and grid metal, and every grid plan in this report adds demand. FCX and other large copper producers are where a price rebound would hit estimates fastest.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Silver is the warning: it closed at 77.85, down 15.27% over 20 sessions despite a 3.05% bounce (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), after a sudden precious-metals sell-off Forbes [Feb 12]. Own gold miners and copper, not silver beta.

Narrative: XLRE closed at 43.50, up 3.60% over five sessions and 4.32% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), riding the 18 bps five-observation drop in the 10Y to 4.04% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13). Duration relief is the driver.

Reported: NNN REIT reported annual results with initial 2026 guidance PR Newswire [Feb 11] — landlord numbers are steady. The volatility came from the AI-scare trade spreading into real estate Reuters [Feb 13], where intermediaries and office owners are exposed, not landlords with long leases.
EPS Upside Watch: Data-centre and net-lease landlords benefit twice — from lower yields and from hyperscaler demand for powered space — and are where 2026 guidance has room to rise.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Existing-home sales tanked more than 8% in January despite lower rates CNBC [Feb 12]: lower yields lift REIT multiples but are not reviving transactions. Own data-centre and net-lease REITs, avoid office and transaction-driven brokers.

Narrative: XLU closed at 46.50, up 2.76% in the prior session, 7.27% over five and 6.63% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13): utilities are bid both as bond proxies and as AI infrastructure. Duke claims the largest spending plan of any regulated US utility at $103B Utility Dive [Feb 12].

Reported: Rate-base growth is the reported story — capex plans keep rising, and the market is paying for them. NextEra closed at 93.80, up 14.13% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

EPS Upside Watch: Merchant generators carry the leverage: Constellation rose 4.46% and Vistra 5.14% in the prior session, and Vistra is up 14.59% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13) — the names most leveraged to data-centre power demand.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Affordability is the political ceiling: electricity prices are rising at double the rate of inflation CNBC [Feb 12]. Regulated rate bases are safer than merchant upside if regulators push data-centre costs back onto the builders.

Narrative: The SXAP tracker closed at 46.31, up 3.69% over five sessions but only 1.23% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Tariffs and Chinese competition are compressing margins faster than cost programmes respond, so rallies look like short-covering, not re-rating.

Reported: Mercedes' full-year earnings more than halved on $1.2 billion of tariff costs CNBC [Feb 12], and S&P and Moody's cut Stellantis to the lowest investment grade Reuters [Feb 10]. Mercedes closed at 57.62, down 2.04% over 20 sessions, and Stellantis' US line at 7.75, down 22.65% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

EPS Upside Watch: Renault is where relief shows, up 6.25% over five sessions, and Volkswagen is up 1.68% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13): volume makers with active cost programmes have the most room for estimate stability.

⚡ Breaking Convention: China's car market is shrinking at the fastest pace in nearly two years Reuters [Feb 10], so German premium brands are fighting for a smaller pool of Chinese buyers. BMW's 1.35% prior-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13) does not change the arithmetic.

Narrative: SOXX closed at 354.66, up 5.17% over 20 sessions, with Micron up 22.29% and TSMC up 7.24% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). The memory squeeze is the profit engine — rampant AI demand for memory is fuelling a growing chip crisis Bloomberg.com [Feb 15].

Reported: Applied Materials jumped after earnings as its CEO made a bold prediction for the chip sector MarketWatch [Feb 12], consistent with equipment demand following memory prices. ASML closed at 1,406.61, up 5.63% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

EPS Upside Watch: Memory and equipment carry the strongest price momentum; AMD, at 207.32 and down 9.04% over 20 sessions, and Intel, down 7.51% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), are the laggards where expectations are now low.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Nvidia is the laggard inside a winning sector, down 2.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13) and stalled despite $600 billion of AI capex TradingView [Feb 13]. The market is paying the bottlenecks (memory, tools), not the platform — until Nvidia's results reset that.

Rewarded: Results that show AI as demand rather than threat: Applied Materials jumped MarketWatch [Feb 12] and Siemens rose on a lifted outlook WSJ [Feb 12]. Self-help with credible guidance also paid — Airbnb rose on a revenue beat and rosy guidance CNBC [Feb 12].

Punished: Beats did not protect anyone whose outlook is clouded by AI or tariffs: Cisco fell 7% despite topping estimates CNBC [Feb 11], Dassault Systèmes plunged 18% CNBC [Feb 11] and Pinterest sank nearly 17% CNBC [Feb 13]. Payout cuts were punished even in the market's strongest sector — BP fell 7% after suspending its buyback Reuters [Feb 10].

Pattern: The market pays for capacity and pricing power (memory, semicap, automation, grid) and fines revenue earned per seat, per transaction or per ad click. Guidance outranks the quarter, and a capital-return cut outranks both. Over 20 sessions the gap shows up on the card: Micron up 22.29% and Caterpillar 19.63%, against Microsoft down 12.12% and Amazon 16.54% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

Attention into EPS: Walmart and fresh economic data lead the week ahead Reuters [Feb 15]; Hims & Hers reports on February 23 HIMS investor relations [Feb 02]; and Nvidia's Feb. 25 date has Wall Street giving a nearly unanimous answer on buying beforehand The Motley Fool [Feb 13]. In Australia, 80 companies prepare to report AFR [Feb 15] — the first large sample of how a higher cash rate and a strong AUD hit guidance.

Playbook: Buy beats with raised guides in physical-AI, grid and memory; fade beats with flat guides in seat-based software, payments and ad platforms until the AI-proof baskets outperform. Use Walmart Reuters [Feb 15] as the test of the defensive rotation: a beat that still sells off means staples are exhausted and the next leg is a rotation back toward beaten-down growth.

Attention Gap: Venezuela is read as a crude-supply headline, yet the cleaner equity lever is refining: the US eased sanctions to give majors broad scope to operate Reuters [Feb 13], which puts more heavy crude within reach of Gulf Coast plants built to process it. Attention has gone to the majors — XLE is up 14.16% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13) — not to the refiners that capture the discount.

Exposure & Risk: Express through Valero and other complex Gulf Coast refiners or a refining ETF (CRAK) rather than more XLE. Risk: an Iran disruption would lift crude faster than product margins, and an OPEC+ output restart from April Reuters [Feb 13] would narrow the heavy-crude discount refiners are counting on.

Attention Gap: DXY closed at 96.88, down 2.46% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), yet the debate is still about gold and the yen. Bloomberg notes carry and commodities make EM currencies more stable than the G-7 Bloomberg.com [Feb 15] — the asset class is being rehabilitated as a volatility diversifier, not just a yield pickup.

Exposure & Risk: Instruments: EMLC for local-currency EM debt, a basket of high-carry Asian and CEE currencies including PLN, and CNH, with USD/CNY already down 0.95% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Risk: a yen carry unwind or a hawkish turn at the Fed would hit carry quickly; size it so a 3% adverse move is survivable.

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 68,788.19, down 1.40% on the day and 22.07% over 20 sessions; ether closed at 1,966.04 (down 5.75% on the day, 32.82% over 20 sessions) and Solana at 86.01 (up 3.73% over five sessions, down 30.72% over 20) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-15). The equity proxies bounced hard on Friday — IBIT up 5.18%, Coinbase up 16.46%, Strategy up 8.85% — but remain down 27.83%, 31.33% and 21.67% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

New / Most Important: Bitcoin shorts reached their most extreme level since the 2024 bottom Yahoo Finance [Feb 14], and bitcoin clawed back to $70,000 after an $8.7 billion wipeout CoinDesk [Feb 14]. Extreme short positioning after a liquidation flush is the classic setup for a squeeze, but ether's 5.75% weekend drop (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-15) shows the bid is narrow and bitcoin-only.

Playbook: Positioning is washed out, the trend is not. Buy IBIT only on a daily bitcoin close back above $70,000 CoinDesk [Feb 14], and step aside if bitcoin loses its five-session range; the 20-session reference of 88,267.14 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-15) shows how much overhead supply sits above. Prefer bitcoin over ether until ETH stops underperforming, and treat MSTR and COIN as short-dated options on a squeeze, not as core holdings.

Rates & Dollar: DXY closed at 96.88, down 2.46% over 20 sessions, while TLT rose 2.49% over five sessions to 89.72 and IEF 1.19% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). The curve did the work: the 10Y fell 18 bps over five observations to 4.04%, and the 2s10s sits at +64 bps in a bull steepening (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13). A falling dollar alongside falling yields is a growth-scare-lite signal, not a funding stress.

Credit Check: HYG closed at 80.85 (down 0.23% over 20 sessions) and LQD at 111.59 (up 0.63%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13): spreads are holding while equity volatility rises. Supply is the story — Alphabet placed almost $32 billion of bonds Bloomberg.com [Feb 10], and investment grade is absorbing AI capex without strain. If stress comes, it will show first in high-yield software borrowers, not in the hyperscalers' paper.

Portfolio Implication: Rotate from US large-cap growth into duration and non-US equities, following the flow: Europe and Asia led equity fund inflows as the US recorded a weekly outflow Reuters [Feb 13]. Hold investment grade at benchmark, underweight high-yield software borrowers and BDCs. Revisit if HYG extends its 20-session decline while TLT stops rallying — that combination would mark a credit event rather than an equity rotation.

What Is Priced: Washington is escalating — the US military is preparing for potentially weeks-long Iran operations Reuters [Feb 15] — while Iran says it is ready to discuss compromises to reach a nuclear deal BBC [Feb 15], and, according to a source, separate Iran and Ukraine talks are set for Tuesday in Geneva The New Arab [Feb 14]. Oil prices little of this: Brent sits at 67.75, up 6.26% over 20 sessions, and the VIX at 20.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

Conditional Expression: If strikes begin: Brent call spreads, XLE and tanker owners, long gold (already up 9.14% over 20 sessions at 5,046.30) and short airlines (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13); the OPEC+ April restart Reuters [Feb 13] caps the move only if Gulf flows are untouched. If Geneva yields a framework: fade the energy premium — XLE's 14.16% 20-session gain is the unwind candidate — and add European cyclicals and EM oil importers (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

Risk: Both outcomes are headline-driven and can reverse within a session; a limited operation could still disrupt shipping, and a deal could stall after an initial relief rally. Keep both legs in options rather than cash positions, and size for gap risk on Asian opens.

What Is Priced: Ukraine-Russia talks are set for Tuesday in Geneva alongside the Iran track The New Arab [Feb 14]. Polish and European assets already price a constructive path: EPOL is up 4.2% over 20 sessions, USD/PLN down 2.12% and the STOXX 600 up 0.54% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), while gas at 3.24 on Henry Hub shows no energy-stress premium in the US.

Conditional Expression: Progress: long European cyclicals and autos (SXAP), PLN and Polish banks, and short European gas exposure; trim defence winners. Breakdown: defence and the SAFE-funded Polish supply chain re-rate higher and PLN gives back gains — hedge with EUR/PLN calls and own European defence primes.

Risk: Europe's own security exposure stays unresolved whatever is agreed in Geneva, so a 'peace' framework could still support European defence budgets, and any deal could stall in EU capitals after an initial relief rally. Size the cyclical leg modestly until terms are public.

Catalyst & Thesis: Walmart's results lead the week ahead Reuters [Feb 15]. The K-shaped consumer favours the scale grocer: the wealthy keep spending while budget shoppers struggle Reuters [Feb 11], so Walmart gains trips at both ends, and the AI scare keeps money hunting for defensive growth.

Price Hurdle & Risk: WMT closed at 133.89, up 12.32% over 20 sessions and 2.07% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), so the bar is high. Express with a call spread rather than stock; exit if the shares fall on a beat, which would signal the staples rotation is spent.

Catalyst & Thesis: The Motley Fool frames Feb. 25 as the decision point, saying Wall Street is providing a nearly unanimous answer on buying Nvidia beforehand The Motley Fool [Feb 13]. The thesis: the stock has stalled despite $600 billion of AI capex TradingView [Feb 13], so expectations sit below the demand signal, and a guide that confirms hyperscaler spending can re-rate the platform the market has been ignoring in favour of memory and tools.

Price Hurdle & Risk: NVDA closed at 182.81, down 2.21% in the prior session and 2.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13); a reclaim of 187.05, its level 20 sessions ago, confirms the call. Risks: margin pressure from memory costs and any sign that customers are stretching capex with debt rather than cash flow.

Catalyst & Thesis: Hims & Hers reports on February 23 HIMS investor relations [Feb 02], with hedge funds betting big against it before a Wegovy showdown Reuters [Feb 13]. The cash-pay obesity niche looks exposed: after its bleak 2026 forecast Yahoo Finance UK [Feb 04], Novo has every incentive to fight for cash-pay patients, and branded price competition erodes the compounding model's discount.

Price Hurdle & Risk: No card price; use defined-risk put spreads into the print rather than an outright short. The danger is the crowding itself: a clean beat or a partnership headline could squeeze shorts violently, so cut the position on any upside guidance revision.

Observed Attention: Yahoo Finance asks whether SanDisk, up 163% in 2026, can be the market's top performer in back-to-back years Yahoo Finance [Feb 14]. MU closed at 411.66, up 22.29% over 20 sessions and 4.3% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

Motivation & Bias: Extrapolation of a price spike — rampant AI demand for memory is fuelling a chip crisis Bloomberg.com [Feb 15] — plus the story that memory is the AI winner software is not. Recency bias underrates how fast supply answers when prices spike.

Instrument & Risk: Hold MU over SNDK and trim into extensions; the 0.56% dip in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13) is the kind of pause that turns into a sharp drawdown when the first capacity announcement lands. Use trailing stops rather than averaging up.

Observed Attention: 24/7 Wall St. called leveraged AGQ the most hated investment it has seen 24/7 Wall St. [Feb 09], and a sudden precious-metals sell-off followed Forbes [Feb 12]. SLV closed at 69.72, down 16.32% over 20 sessions despite a 2.94% bounce in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

Motivation & Bias: A debasement narrative plus bottom-fishing after a crash: retail treats a 15% drawdown as a discount rather than as evidence of a broken trend. Gold's 9.14% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13) feeds the 'silver must catch up' argument.

Instrument & Risk: Leveraged AGQ's daily-reset decay punishes holders in a choppy range. If you must, hold SLV with a hard stop, or use gold (GLD up 9.28% over 20 sessions) as the lower-volatility substitute (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

Observed Attention: Coinbase jumped 16.46% and Strategy 8.85% on Friday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), as Coinbase's CEO said he is 'more bullish than ever' through the downturn Yahoo Finance [Feb 13].

Motivation & Bias: Short-squeeze chasing after bitcoin shorts hit their most extreme level since 2024 Yahoo Finance [Feb 14]; anchoring on old highs ignores that both stocks remain far below their levels of 20 sessions ago.

Instrument & Risk: COIN at 164.32 is still down 31.33% over 20 sessions and MSTR at 133.88 down 21.67% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Prefer IBIT for direction and size MSTR and COIN as options, since equity issuance and crypto-volume swings amplify every move in the coin.
Observed Attention: The WSJ says Robinhood got a prediction-market lift despite its cooling crypto business WSJ [Feb 10] — a sign retail activity is shifting from coins toward event contracts.

Motivation & Bias: Quick resolution and lottery-style payoffs — the same impulse that drove meme coins, now in a regulated wrapper. The cohort is active, just rotating toward faster bets as crypto prices fall.

Instrument & Risk: HOOD is the listed proxy (no card price). Regulatory scrutiny of event contracts and new competitors entering the space could compress take rates, and crypto volumes remain a drag — keep it a trading position, not a core holding.
